none: verse quotation and introductory transition only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī refutes the claim that idols confer honor because worshippers can approach, see, and present their needs to them.
rows.anchor: إبطالا لما كانوا يقولون إن في عبادة الأصنام عزة من حيث القرب منها والنظر إليها وعرض الحوائج عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols do not hear their callers, whereas God receives and accepts the good word that ascends to Him.
rows.anchor: فقال هؤلاء لا يسمعون دعاءكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even granting the idolaters’ belief that idols hear and know, they cannot claim that idols answer prayers, since nonresponse is perceptible while hearing is a rational dispute.
rows.anchor: فإنهم كانوا يقولون بأن الأصنام تسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing idols give no worldly benefit, God shows that they will bring no afterlife benefit and will instead disavow their worshippers’ association.
rows.anchor: لما بين عدم النفع فيهم في الدنيا بين عدم النفع منهم في الآخرة بل أشار إلى وجود الضرر منهم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here shirk means associating something with God, as in the description of association as a tremendous wrong.
rows.anchor: أي بإشراككم بالله شيئا ، كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading addresses the Prophet: God reveals that wood and stone will speak and disavow their worshippers on Judgment Day, something reason alone could not know; the extraordinary report is true because its source is all-knowing.
rows.anchor: أن الخشب والحجر يوم القيامة ينطق ويكذب عابده وذلك أمر لا يعلم بالعقل المجرد لولا إخبار الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the address is general: whoever the listener may be, what has just been related is true, and none informs like an expert.
rows.anchor: أيها السامع كائنا من كنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against disbelievers who suggested God urgently commands worship because He needs it, Rāzī says worship is commanded for human care, not divine need.
rows.anchor: لما كثر الدعاء من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والإصرار من الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although predicates are usually indefinite, a definite predicate is apt when both facts are known and the statement reminds rather than informs; everyone already knows humans are needy.
rows.anchor: فإن كان الخبر معلوما عند السامع والمبتدأ كذلك ويقع الخبر تنبيها لا تفهيما يحسن تعريف الخبر غاية الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase teaches that dependence and reliance belong to God alone, requiring worship of Him and excluding worship of anything on which people do not depend.
rows.anchor: إعلام بأنه لا افتقار إلا إليه ولا اتكال إلا عليه وهذا يوجب عبادته لكونه مفتقرا إليه وعدم عبادة غيره لعدم الافتقار إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though wholly self-sufficient, God calls people repeatedly, while they remain needy yet fail to answer or call upon Him for a response.
rows.anchor: أي هو مع استغنائه يدعوكم كل الدعاء وأنتم من احتياجكم لا تجيبونه ولا تدعونه فيجيبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding “to God” emphasizes exclusive worship; adding “Praiseworthy” to “rich” signals that His favors merit gratitude and worship.
rows.anchor: إشارة لوجوب حصر العبادة في عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human poverty is not matched by divine poverty: God is absolutely rich, meets people’s worldly needs, and will meet believers’ needs in the next life.
rows.anchor: بل هو غني على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses “when the messengers came” as an appositive to “the people of the town,” making the parable refer to that time.
rows.anchor: إذ منصوبة لأنها بدل من أصحاب القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Rāzī’s reading of the parable as consolation for Muhammad, the time phrase may instead modify “strike a parable”: set it at the messengers’ arrival.
rows.anchor: وعلى قولنا إن هذا المثل مضروب لنفس محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town is Antioch and its three messengers were from Jesus’ followers, the nearest messengers to the people before Muhammad’s time.
rows.anchor: والقرية أنطاكية والمرسلون من قوم عيسى وهم أقرب مرسل أرسل إلى قوم إلى زمان محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وهم ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible parsing makes “when We sent” an appositive to “when they came,” describing the parable as the sending to the town’s people.
rows.anchor: أن يكون إذ أرسلنا بدلا من إذ جاءها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers the clearer parsing in which the time clause modifies “they came”: the messengers came when God sent them, not on their own initiative.
rows.anchor: وهو الأصح والأوضح أن يكون إذ ظرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the messengers were sent by Jesus, God calls their commission His own: an authorized messenger of God’s messenger is also God’s messenger, consoling Muhammad that rejection of them equals rejection of him.
rows.anchor: إرسال عيسى عليه السلام هو إرسالنا ورسول رسول الله بإذن الله رسول الله فلا يقع لك يا محمد أن أولئك كانوا رسل الرسول وأنت رسول الله فإن تكذيبهم كتكذيبك فتتم التسلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This supports the legal principle that an agent appointed with the principal’s permission is the principal’s agent, removable by the principal but not by the intermediate agent.
rows.anchor: وهذا يؤيد مسألة فقهية وهي أن وكيل الوكيل بإذن الموكل وكيل الموكل لا وكيل الوكيل حتى لا ينعزل بعزل الوكيل إياه وينعزل إذا عزله الموكل الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers’ statement that only delivery was incumbent on them both consoles them and prompts reflection: they seek no wage or power, only preaching and reminder.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك يوجب تفكرهم في أمرهم حيث لم يطلبوا منهم أجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense of clear delivery is distinguishing truth from falsehood through miracle and proof.
rows.anchor: البلاغ المبين للحق عن الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means making the message manifest to everyone; merely conveying it to one or two people is insufficient.
rows.anchor: البلاغ المظهر لما أرسلنا للكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third sense is clarifying the truth by every available means; if people then refuse, destruction becomes deserved.
rows.anchor: البلاغ المظهر للحق بكل ما يمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents escalate as the messengers intensify their preaching: after rejecting their claim and oath, they answer with another assertion, this time accusing them of ill omen.
rows.anchor: ولما أكد الرسل قولهم باليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their superstition treats the messengers as a renewed cause of misfortune, invoking the proverb that a false oath leaves homes desolate.
rows.anchor: اليمين الكاذبة تدع الديار بلاقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We will stone you” may mean verbally curse or insult you; then “painful punishment” escalates the threat to physical beating and pain.
rows.anchor: لنشتمنكم منا لرجم بالقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they threaten actual stoning, with the following phrase explaining that they will continue pelting the messengers until death, making the punishment painful.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد الرجم بالحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes alīm as “pain-causing,” with the rare pattern فعيل functioning like مفعل.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرنا في الأليم أنه بمعنى لمؤلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, alīm means “possessing pain,” with فعيل functioning as فاعل, a common pattern like “an evening that is pleased” in 69:21.
rows.anchor: فالعذاب الأليم هو ذو ألم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assembly of idolaters and idols signals resurrection after the affirmation of monotheism; Rāzī connects it to 21:98, 37:22–23, and 34:38.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الحشر بعد تقرير التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reading is that the worshippers themselves are an army for the gods they adopted.
rows.anchor: أن يكون العابدون جندا لما اتخذوه آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes the idols an army for their worshippers; Rāzī draws out the point that they still cannot defend them despite being assembled for that purpose.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الأصنام جندا للعابدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An assembled force that is present yet cannot aid its allies displays extreme weakness, more than a force that never gathered or prepared.
rows.anchor: فإن من حضر واجتمع ثم عجز عن النصرة

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh treat لات as lā resembling laysa with an added feminine tāʾ for emphasis; it applies only to times and normally exposes only its subject or predicate, not both.
rows.anchor: الخليل وسيبويه أن لات هي لا المشبهة بليس زيدت عليها تاء التأنيث كما زيدت على رب وثم للتأكيد

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash instead analyzes لات as the general negative particle lā plus tāʾ, specialized to negate times; ḥīna manāṣ is accusative under it or nominative with an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش إنها لا النافية للجنس

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers pause on the tāʾ of لات.
rows.anchor: الجمهور يقفون على التاء من قوله

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī pauses with hāʾ, as with feminine nouns.
rows.anchor: والكسائي يقف عليها بالهاء

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshāf rejects Abū ʿUbayda’s claim that the tāʾ belongs to ḥīn; its placement beside ḥīn in the ʿUthmānic codex proves little because codex spelling can depart from analogy.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : وأما قول أب يعبيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manāṣ means escape or aid: nāṣahu means he aided him, and istanāṣa means he sought escape.
rows.anchor: المناص المنجا والغوث ، يثال ناصه

rows.speaker: الكفار
rows.claim: One explanation is that they objected that Muhammad matched them in outward and inward qualities, lineage, appearance, and form, so they wondered how he alone received such rank.
rows.anchor: والأخلاق الباطنة والنسب والشكل والصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “from among them” underscores their ignorance: a man calls them to monotheism, honoring angels, the afterlife, and turning from worldly life, though they know he avoided lies; all of this should make them believe.
rows.anchor: من هذه الكلمة لا التنبيه على كمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Muhammad shared their clan and worldly circumstances, their refusal to obey and their amazement at his distinction had no cause except envy.
rows.anchor: فما كان لهذا التعجب سبب إلا الحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “the disbelievers said,” rather than “they said,” heightens the astonishment and marks the accusation as speech born only of complete disbelief.
rows.anchor: إظهارا للتعجب ودلالة على أن هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Muhammad a sorcerer and liar is incoherent: a sorcerer turns people from God to Satan, whereas Muhammad calls to God and reports truths established by reason, including resurrection.
rows.anchor: فإن الساحر هو الذي يمنع من طاعة الله ويدعو إلى طاعة الشيطان وهو عندكم بالعكس من ذلك والكذاب هو الذي يخبر عن الشيء لا على ما هو عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī groups the disbelievers’ attempted proofs of Muhammad’s falsehood under theology, prophethood, and the resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهي ثلاثة أشياء أحدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī cites an ungraded report: after ʿUmar converted and Muslims rejoiced, Quraysh chiefs asked Abū Ṭālib to arbitrate; Muhammad offered the testimony of God’s oneness in return for their support, and they left in protest.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما أسلم عمر فرح به المسلمون فرحا شديدا

rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: Their first argument assumes from visible experience that one agent cannot have the capacity and knowledge to preserve a vast creation, so many gods must each maintain a different kind.
rows.anchor: أن القوم ما كانوا من أصحاب النظر والاستدلال بل كانت أوهامهم تابعة للمحسوسات فلما وجدوا في الشاهد أن الفاعل الواحد لا تفي قدرته وعلمه بحفظ الخلق العظيم

rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: Their other objection appeals to numerous, supposedly intelligent forebears who rejected monotheism, contrasted with one man claiming to be right.
rows.anchor: لكثرتهم وقوة عقولهم كانوا جاهلين مبطلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If unproved analogy from the visible to the unseen were valid, the polytheists’ first argument would stand; the same reasoning underlies anthropomorphists’ claims about God’s body and place and Muʿtazilite claims about divine acts, so Rāzī rejects those positions’ central analogy too.
rows.anchor: إجراء حكم الشاهد على الغائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal to inherited belief is also invalid: if taqlīd were sound, the disbelievers’ appeal to their ancestors would be sound, but it is false.
rows.anchor: فاسدة علمنا أن التقليد باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjāb means “astonishing” but is a stronger form, like the intensified forms ṭawīl/ṭawwāl, ʿarīḍ/ʿarrāḍ, and kabīr/kabbār; doubling can intensify further.
rows.anchor: أن العجاب هو العجيب إلا أنه أبلغ من العجيب كقولهم طويل وطوال وعريض وعراض وكبير وكبار

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshāf records light and doubled readings of ʿajāb and says the doubled form is more emphatic, as in 71:22.
rows.anchor: عجاب بالتخفيف والتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malaʾ denotes people whose presence fills hearts and eyes with awe and majesty.
rows.anchor: أن لملأ عبارة عن القوم الذين إذا حضروا في المجلس فإنه تمتلىء القلوب والعيون من مهابتهم وعظمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among them” means Quraysh: they left Abū Ṭālib’s council after Muhammad silenced them with a decisive answer, urging one another to persist.
rows.anchor: أي من قريش انطلقوا عن مجلس أبي طالب

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: The common reading has an, while Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads امشوا without it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة امشوا بحذف أن

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshāf takes أن to mean أي (“that is”) because leaving a debate requires the disputants to speak and confer about what happened.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب : ( الكشاف ) ( أن ) بمعنى أي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also credited with the wording وانطبق الملأ منهم يمشون.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس : وانطبق الملأ منهم يمشون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their instruction means to keep going and persevere, since they saw no way to stop Muhammad’s cause.
rows.anchor: أنه قال بعضهم امشوا واصبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that Muhammad’s religion is growing without an apparent cause only because God wills it, and none can repel what God wills.
rows.anchor: ظهور دين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ليس له سبب ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they call the affair one of the calamities of time from which they cannot escape.
rows.anchor: أن الأمر كشيء من نوائب الدهر فلا انفكاك لنا منه

rows.speaker: الفقال
rows.claim: A third reading is a threat: Muhammad seeks to seize their religion and rule over their property and children.
rows.anchor: قال الفقال هذه كلمة تذكر للتهديد والتخويف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-milla al-ākhira may mean Christianity, whose adherents did not teach Muhammad’s monotheism, or Quraysh’s inherited religion.
rows.anchor: والملة الآخرة هي ملة النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the “later religion” means the religion of Quraysh’s own ancestors.
rows.anchor: أو يكون المراد بالمراد بالملة الآخرة ملة قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhtilāq means fabrication and falsehood.
rows.anchor: إن هاذا إلا اختلاق } افتعال وكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inference that monotheism is false because their ancestors never professed it exposes the invalidity of taqlīd: if following ancestors were sound, their polytheist argument would be sound.
rows.anchor: نحن ما سمعنا عن أسلافنا القول بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing proofs for obedience and turning away from worldly life, Rāzī says their benefit is complete only when God opens the chest and illuminates the heart.
rows.anchor: لما بالغ في تقرير البيانات الدالة على وجوب الإقبال على طاعة الله تعالى ووجوب الإعراض عن الدنيا بين بعد ذلك أن الانتفاع بهذه البيانات لا يكمل إلا إذا شرح الله الصدور ونور القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī refers readers to his fuller discussion of chest expansion and guidance under 6:125, while briefly restating it here.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنا بالغنا في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human souls differ essentially: some are noble, luminous, and drawn to spiritual realities, while others are base, turbid, and drawn to bodily life; observation confirms this variation.
rows.anchor: خلق جواهر النفوس مختلفة بالماهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Chest expansion is an innate strong readiness in the soul; when it exists, a slight cause brings it into action, like sulfur ignited by a small flame.
rows.anchor: المراد بشرح الصدر هو ذلك الاستعداد الشديد الموجود في فطرة النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “light” is guidance and knowledge; chest readiness comes first, and its absence leaves a person unable to benefit from proofs, which may instead deepen aversion.
rows.anchor: وأما النور فهو عبارة عن الهداية والمعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a soul is remote from spiritual states and absorbed in bodily desires, repeated proofs lessen its hardness and darkness; these principles are needed to understand the verses.
rows.anchor: كلما كان إيراد الدلائل اليقينية والبراهين الباهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the arguments of his school on determinism and predestination, and the opponents’ responses, were already discussed under 6:125.
rows.anchor: أما استدلال أصحابنا في مسألة الجبر والقدر وكلام الخصوم عليه فقد تقدم هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate after man is omitted, as in 39:9: the opened and guided person is compared with one whose heart is sealed and who is unguided; the following woe supplies the answer.
rows.anchor: من محذوف الخبر كما في قوله

words: فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُم مِّن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because remembrance ordinarily brings light, guidance, and reassurance, Rāzī asks why this verse associates it with hard hearts; he cites 13:28.
rows.anchor: أن ذكر الله سبب لحصول النور والهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For souls of evil, turbid nature that are far from spiritual things and inclined to bestial traits, hearing God’s remembrance can increase hardness and turbidity.
rows.anchor: إن النفس إذا كانت خبيثة الجوهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One agent can affect recipients differently: sunlight darkens a dyer’s face but whitens his cloth, and its heat softens wax while hardening salt; the same speech also pleases one listener and repels another.
rows.anchor: كنور الشمس يسود وجه القصار ويبيض ثوبه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Rāzī reports that when 23:12–14 was recited, ʿUmar and another man both said “Blessed is God, the best of creators”; the Prophet told him to write it as revealed, after which ʿUmar’s faith grew and the other man’s disbelief grew. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus remembrance gives light and reassurance to pure spiritual souls but hardens evil satanic souls; when the chief spiritual medicine worsens an illness, that soul is beyond cure and at the worst degree of evil.
rows.anchor: إذا عرفت هذا لم يبعد أيضا أن يكون ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following discussion describes the Qur’an as light, healing, guidance, and reassurance; its producing greater hardness for such a person shows the soul’s extreme vileness.
rows.anchor: ولما بين تعالى ذلك أردفه بما يدل على أن القرآن سبب لحصول النور والشفاء والهداية وزيادة الاطمئنان
